_readme: TEMPLATE. The real files are infrastructure/secrets/staging.json and infrastructure/secrets/prod.json
(gitignored), created from this one the first time a script needs them. EVERY VALUE MUST DIFFER
between staging and production: a shared jwt_secret lets a staging token authenticate against
production, a shared encryption_key lets a staging dump decrypt production PII.
Who fills what:
database_url (ozari_api, pooled),
direct_database_url (ozari_migrator) ./infrastructure/scripts/neon.ps1 <env>         (automatic)
jwt_secret, jwt_refresh_secret,
encryption_key, api_key             ./infrastructure/scripts/new-secrets.ps1 <env>   (automatic)
email_key                           Resend -> API Keys (one per environment)         secret.ps1
r2_access_key, r2_secret_key        Cloudflare -> R2 -> Manage API tokens -> Account API token
ozari-<env>-assets, Object Read & Write, this bucket only.
The Access Key ID + Secret Access Key (not the cfat_ value)  secret.ps1
google_client_id/_secret            Google Auth Platform -> Clients (DEPLOYMENT.md 3d) secret.ps1
github_oauth_token                  GitHub -> Developer settings -> Tokens (CLASSIC), scopes
repo + read:user. Cloud Build rejects fine-grained tokens.  secret.ps1
rotation: counters, one per secret key. Absent = 1. The scripts bump them when they replace a
value; the next gcp apply then pushes a new Secret Manager version and destroys the old one.
encryption_key is generated ONCE and never rotated while the environment holds data: every
*_kms column becomes unreadable forever. Keep a copy of this file OFF this machine.
